rules.description: An SGID binary targeting the root or shadow group is writable by all users, giving a deterministic path to root-equivalent privileges.
rules.exploit: Overwrite the world-writable binary with attacker-controlled code to gain root or shadow group privileges (e.g. read /etc/shadow) on execution.

rules.description: An SGID binary targeting a group other than root or shadow is writable by all users. Impact depends on what that group can access.
rules.exploit: Overwrite the binary and inspect what resources the target group can access; this may enable a further privilege escalation chain.

rules.description: An SGID binary is located in a user-writable or non-standard location, suggesting it may be a planted or custom binary rather than a distro package.
rules.exploit: Inspect the binary directly (strings, ltrace, or disassembly) to determine what it does and whether it can be leveraged for group privilege escalation.
